result:
All five March AP inbox bills are booked. Summary of what I did:

**Verification first** — before posting I confirmed none of the five were already in the books (reviewed all 12 existing March AP entries), that no accrual in 2100 would double-count them, and that no cash had gone out to any of these vendors (checked all unmatched US bank lines). All five are Net 30 and unpaid at 3/31, so all correctly credit AP.

**Three straightforward March expenses:**
- JE-00304 Quillon Analytics $2,180 → 6200 Software Subscriptions
- JE-00305 Cirrus CDN $7,940.55 → 5000 Hosting & Infrastructure
- JE-00306 Whitcombe & Ames $3,475 → 6500 Legal Fees

**Two that needed prepaid treatment under Policy §4 — the real judgment calls:**
- **JE-00307 Delmar Insurance $9,600** — D&O premium covering 3/1/26–2/28/27. Split: $800 to 6700 Insurance (1 of 12 months) and $8,800 to 1220 Prepaid Insurance.
- **JE-00308 Meridian Events $4,200** — booth deposit for a June 2026 expo. Deposits for future events go to 1200 Prepaid Expenses and expense when the event occurs, so **no March P&L hit at all**.

Booking those last two straight to expense would have overstated March expenses by $13,000.

**Notes on policy compliance:** every entry is under the $10,000 posting threshold (largest is $9,600), so no controller approval was required. I deliberately recorded Delmar as one entry rather than splitting the prepaid and amortization pieces, since splitting to stay under a threshold is prohibited. No exceptions flagged — all five had invoices as support.

**One thing needing your attention:** I set the US "AP cutoff review" checklist item to *in_progress*, not complete. These five bills are done, but a genuine cutoff review still needs a sweep for March services received but uninvoiced (§5 accruals) and a look at early-April invoices with March service periods. I also left two follow-ups in the memo: adding Delmar to the amortization schedule at $800/month through Feb 2027, and calendaring the Meridian deposit for release in the June close.
